h1:
Hua Hin with Kids
2 Days, 1 Night
intro: Hua Hin is one of the easiest places to bring kids without stressing out. It's only about a 3-hour drive from Bangkok, and you get a big water park, a sheep farm built for photos, a Greek-style village, and a long sandy beach for the kids to run around on. We've put together a relaxed 2-day, 1-night plan where everything is close together and easy to loop, with real timings, current ticket prices, and the spots to watch out for when you're traveling with little ones.

blocks.html: What makes Hua Hin so easy for families is that everything sits along Phetkasem Road. Drive north from town toward Cha-Am and you'll find Santorini Park and Swiss Sheep Farm not far apart, while Vana Nava water park and Khao Takiab beach are just south of the center. You can cover several spots in a single day without long drives. This plan puts the water park and beach on day one, then the sheep farm and Greek village on day two before heading home — feel free to swap the order based on the weather and your kids' mood.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Vana Nava water park, then the beach

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: A full day in the water + the beach at dusk

items.activity: Leave Bangkok and drive down to Hua Hin
items.note: It's about 200 km and takes 3–3.5 hours depending on traffic. You can stop at a service station for breakfast on the way. On a long weekend, leave earlier to beat the mid-morning jams.

items.activity: Arrive at Vana Nava Water Jungle
items.note: Open 11:00–17:00. Adult tickets (122 cm and taller) run around 1,299 THB; kids 111–121 cm tall and seniors 60+ are around 850 THB. Buying ahead on Klook or Trip is usually cheaper than the gate. There's a separate shallow toddler zone away from the big slides.
There are restaurants and a buffet inside, priced higher than outside as you'd expect. To save a bit, you can bring some of your own water and snacks for the kids.

items.activity: Keep playing until closing, then shower and change
items.note: The afternoon sun is strong — reapply sunscreen on the kids every 2 hours. Hats and rash guards help a lot.

items.activity: Check in near Khao Takiab or in the town center
items.note: A beachfront hotel or one with a kids' pool lets them keep playing. Room rates swing a lot by season and long weekends, so book ahead during high season.

items.activity: Evening stroll on Khao Takiab beach
items.note: The Khao Takiab side has gentler waves than the town beach, good for letting kids run along the water. Always check the warning flags before going in — during the monsoon the surf can pick up and there can be jellyfish.

items.activity: Seafood dinner by Khao Takiab beach
items.note: Seafood restaurants line the beach. Pick a busy one for fresher catch, and ask the price per kilo before ordering so there are no surprises.

blocks.title: Beach safety
blocks.html: Hua Hin's beaches are lovely, but the wind and surf pick up in places, especially during monsoon season (roughly May–October). Always check the warning flags before taking kids into the water — a red flag means absolutely no swimming. In the hottest months jellyfish sometimes drift in too, so keep the kids in the shallows and within sight at all times.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Hua Hin trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Swiss Sheep Farm, then Santorini Park

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Sheep farm + Greek village before heading home

items.activity: Breakfast at the hotel, pack up and check out
items.note: Load everything into the car before you set off so you can drive straight back to Bangkok in the afternoon without doubling back.

items.activity: Drive north toward Cha-Am to Swiss Sheep Farm
items.note: It's about 30–40 minutes north of Hua Hin town. Open Mon–Fri 10:00–19:00, Sat–Sun 09:00–19:00. Entry is around 120 THB for adults and 80 THB for kids; children up to 80 cm tall get in free.

items.activity: Feed the sheep, take photos in the European corners
items.note: You can buy feed for the kids to hand to the sheep, which they love. There are plenty of European-countryside photo spots. Go early while the sun is gentler and it's less crowded.

items.activity: Walk over to Santorini Park nearby
items.note: A white-and-blue Greek-style village with amusement rides, shops, and lots of photo spots. Open roughly 09:30–18:00. Entry and ride tickets are sold separately, so you can just walk around for photos without paying for rides.
There are restaurants and cafés inside Santorini, but if you want to save money there are plenty of options out along Phetkasem Road.

items.activity: Stop by a market or café before leaving (if you've got energy)
items.note: On Fri–Sun, Cicada Market near Khao Takiab opens in the evening from 17:00, with puppet shows and an open space for kids to run around. But if you want to be home before nightfall, save it for next trip.
The drive back is 3–3.5 hours. Avoid leaving after 17:00 on a Sunday, when the return traffic into Bangkok gets very heavy.

blocks.text: Family-friendly spots in Hua Hin worth knowing

items.name: Vana Nava Water Jungle
items.blurb: A big water park in Hua Hin town with a range of slides and a clearly separated shallow toddler zone. Easily a full day, and a great anchor activity for the trip.

items.name: Swiss Sheep Farm Cha-Am
items.blurb: A European-styled sheep farm where you can feed the sheep and shoot photos in countryside corners. Little kids love getting close to feed the animals. Plan on about 1–1.5 hours.

items.name: Santorini Park Cha-Am
items.blurb: A white-and-blue Greek-style village with an amusement park, rides, shops, and plenty of photo spots. Pleasant to wander and shoot photos; ride tickets are bought separately.

items.name: Khao Takiab Beach
items.blurb: Hua Hin's southern beach, with gentler waves than the town beach and a laid-back feel. There are seafood spots along the sand, and it's good for kids to build sandcastles and splash in the shallows.
items.meta: South of Hua Hin town · near Khao Takiab

items.name: Cicada Market
items.blurb: A craft market near Khao Takiab with a big open space for kids to run, plus puppet shows and stage performances. Eat and shop for handmade goods.

items.name: Plearnwan
items.blurb: A retro village with an old-Thai feel, full of vintage snacks and toys. Fun to wander and photograph, and a good short stop during the day.
items.meta: Between Hua Hin and Cha-Am, Phetkasem Rd

items.name: Hua Hin Town Beach
items.blurb: A long beach right in the center, walkable from the market and restaurants, with horseback rides along the sand. Waves can be stronger here than at Khao Takiab, so check the flags before going in.

items.name: Bluport Hua Hin
items.blurb: An air-conditioned mall in the center with a cinema, restaurants, and a kids' zone. A solid place to escape the heat or duck out of an afternoon shower when you're with little ones.

blocks.text: How to prep when traveling with kids

items: Sunscreen and hats — the Hua Hin sun is strong at both the water park and the beach. Reapply sunscreen every 2 hours and pack rash guards for the kids.
Swimsuits + towels — day one uses both the water park and the beach, so bring spare outfits and a bag for wet things.
Drinking water and snacks — food inside the water park and amusement park costs more than outside, so packing some water and kids' snacks helps save money.
Watch out for monkeys at Khao Takiab — the Khao Takiab side has lots of monkeys. Don't flash food bags, and keep glasses, phones, and snacks tucked away — the monkeys will snatch things.
Book accommodation ahead — on long weekends rooms fill fast and prices spike. Booking early gets you a better rate and your pick of family rooms.

blocks.text: Getting to and around Hua Hin

blocks.html: Bangkok to Hua Hin is about 200 km, a 3–3.5 hour self-drive that's the most convenient option for families — you can loop between spots on your own schedule and have somewhere to stash your gear. If you're not driving, vans and coaches from Bangkok start in the low hundreds of THB per person, and there's a train too, though it takes around 4 hours. Once you're in Hua Hin, having your own car or a rental is far more flexible since the attractions are spread along Phetkasem Road. There are songthaews and taxis in town, but they're less convenient when you're traveling with kids and a lot of luggage.

blocks.title: Pricing to keep in mind
blocks.html: Water park tickets, room rates, and transport all swing quite a bit by season and long weekends. The figures in this article are rough off-peak prices, so check the actual rates in your booking app before you go. Buying water park tickets online ahead of time usually beats the gate price.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Hua Hin with young kids?
faq.a: Two days and one night is just about right. Spend day one at Vana Nava water park and hit the beach in the evening, then cover Swiss Sheep Farm and Santorini Park on day two before driving home. If you'd rather take it slow or add the Cicada night market, staying two nights is more relaxing.

faq.q: Is Hua Hin beach safe for kids to swim?
faq.a: Mostly safe and shallow, especially on the Khao Takiab side where the waves are gentler. But during monsoon season (roughly May–October) the surf gets stronger and there can be jellyfish at times. Always check the warning flags before going in — a red flag means no swimming — and keep kids within sight at all times.

faq.q: How much are Vana Nava water park tickets?
faq.a: Standard prices are around 1,299 THB for adults (122 cm and taller), and around 850 THB for kids 111–121 cm tall and seniors 60 and over. It's open 11:00–17:00. Buying ahead online via Klook or Trip is usually cheaper than the gate.

faq.q: Are Swiss Sheep Farm and Santorini Park close together?
faq.a: Yes, they're close together near Cha-Am, about 30–40 minutes north of Hua Hin town, and it's a short hop between the two. You can easily do both back to back in half a day, so plan them for the same day.

faq.q: When's the best time to visit Hua Hin with the family?
faq.a: November to February has the best weather — little rain and calm seas, great for letting kids swim. Monsoon season from May to October still works, but watch for surf and rain. Avoid long weekends if you'd rather skip the crowds and high room prices.
